author: DavidG389
text: Hey Sean I am back testing SPY as well.  I did the 5 miute ORB and the Premarket High Low and have been trying to stay very strict.  My limits are entry at the top of the body of the retested candle if the next candle clears that point.  My stop is a $.50 stop loss and a 1 to 2 RR.  If the high of day hits before the 2R I will sell half.  If the 2R won't go past the high of day because of moves earlier in the day were higher I just hold till the 2 R and sell the whole position.  I have backtested from June of 25 till March of 26.  Its been a little tedious but have gotten good results.  Now I am working through PDH and PDL.  Good luck, drop me a message and let me know how its working.

author: Metamorphosis
text:
<@613464484350132250> ,I’ve had a look, and the concept looks really promising.

One feature that would make it even more powerful is the ability to include multiple indexes in the table. Traders like myself often use both SPY and QQQ correlation to gauge the strength and direction of the market.

It would also be great to have the ability to filter stocks based on whether they're above or below key levels such as PDH/PDL, PMH/PML, etc., with the option to apply these filters simultaneously to narrow down only the stocks that meet all the selected criteria.

Another useful addition would be the ability to customise the ORB timeframe to whatever the user prefers. It would also be helpful to filter stocks based on whether price is above or below the ORB range, with a simple visual indicator in the table, similar to the PDH/PDL symbols.

Finally, it would be great to include VWAP and EMA/SMA in the table, again using simple symbols to show whether price is above or below each level, along with the ability to apply those filters simultaneously.

Overall, I think the concept is excellent. These additions would make it an incredibly powerful tool for traders who use index correlation, key price levels, ORB, VWAP, and moving averages to identify high-probability setups.

Thanks for your effort.

author: kalerv
text:
Hey, thanks for the detailed feedback — genuinely useful to hear how other traders are thinking about this.

Before jumping into building, I want to make sure anything added actually improves decisions rather than just adding more to look at. A few honest questions:

On multiple benchmarks: When SPY and QQQ are pointing in different directions on a given day, what do you actually do differently? Do you trade both signals, pick the stronger one, or sit out entirely? Asking because two RS columns that sometimes disagree might create more confusion than clarity — want to understand your actual process before wiring it in.

On ORB timeframe: What timeframe do you use and why that one specifically? And when price is sitting between the ORB high and low, do you pass on the trade or just note it as context? If it’s a hard filter for you, that’s worth building. If it’s just nice to see, it probably doesn’t need its own column.

On VWAP/EMA: Can you walk me through a recent trade where VWAP or an EMA specifically changed your decision — not just confirmed it, but actually changed it? The concern here is that these are session-anchor or HTF references, and this tool is designed to find intraday relative strength right now. Adding HTF filters risks answering a different question than the one the tool is built for.

On filtering: Agreed it sounds useful, but a stock that’s “Inside” at 9:40 and filtered out might be your best trade at 10:15. The color coding already lets you scan for what meets criteria without hiding names you might need later.

The core goal of this tool is one thing: at any point during the session, which names are genuinely leading or lagging the market right now — not just historically, not just structurally, but in the tape. Everything in scope needs to serve that question directly.

What does your actual pre-trade checklist look like step by step? That would help figure out where this fits and what, if anything, is genuinely missing.

Lots of red folder this week so expect lots of volatility. What I would like to see coming into today is for the dips to get bought up on the SPY and QQQ. SPY I would like to see a hold of 600.87 on the higher timeframes and QQQ I would like to see the hold of 509.8. 

As for the other tickers I would like to see TSLA hold 349 on the higher timeframes. This is going to be my main watch coming into today. 

AMZN also looks really good as well. I would like to see the hold of 207,208 retest for continuations higher. 

AAPL is at ATH's I would be careful on this one as its in a very key area. 

As for the other tickers look for Relative strength/weakness intraday. Most of these tickers are just going to do what the SPY and QQQ does.

Gameplan January 30th 

Markets are in a key spot. QQQ looks really good for a move back towards the gap fill if we can hold the PDH and the 523 level. SPY I would like to see the reaction off the 605. Coming into today I would like to see the market create a higher low from yesterday and move back towards the upside. 

With the FOMC coming in with a bunch of earnings as well not dropping the market this means that if we can maintain levels we will move hgiher. 

As for the tech names like TSLA, META and MSFT. I would be very cautious right off of the bat. Wait for and IV flush the contracts are going to get ruined on both sides. 

Names that I'm looking for today will be NVDA. Tighter range here. I would like to see the break of either side for a move towards PDH or PDL. AMZN looks good if we can hold the PDL level. I also like GOOG for a hold of the PDH for a push back towards the GAp fill. NFLX also looks good for a move higher if we can get above the 986 on the higher timeframes.

text:
Gameplan February 3rd 

Start of the month. Gap down over the weekend with the tariffs news. As I mentioned this is a news driven market. Any headlines are going to move the markets to either side. Be cautious and don't be over exposed especially on overnight positions. 

SPY and QQQ are gapping down fairly big here. What I would like to see is the reaction that we have within the first 10-15 minutes of market open. As I mentioned do not have bias coming into the market open. Be open to playing both side. Things move quickly in this market. 

As for my main watches they will be NVDA. This one is gapping down I would like to see the retest of the 117 level on the higher timeframes. I will be looking for a pop and fade on this name coming into market open. 

TSLA I would like to see the reaction around the 386 area, AAPL the 230 area, META the 680 area. 

As for AMD, AMZN and, GOOG. These ones have earnings this week so keep this in mind if you are going to trade them. 

@everyone

text:
Gameplan February 5th 

Coming into today we do have a mini gap down on the overall markets right back inside key levels on the higher timeframes. What I would like to see is the reaction within the first 10-15 minutes on the overall markets. We also do have some red folder news at 10:00AM. 

Lots of conflicting moves. We have some names that are holding up compared to some names that have bad earnings and are dropping. Really want to focus in a few tickers coming into market open. 

The main watches will be a potential earnings play right off the bat on AMD and GOOG. I want to see an IV flush and we can look for the pop and fade right off of the bat. 

If those don't setup then we will be patient and wait for the indices and the overall tech to give up a clear direction in the markets. 

TSLA, NVDA, & AAPL are the ones to keep an eye out on. I laid out the gameplan in the pre market. The levels have been set as well. Now we just wait and see the reaction we have around those levels. 

As for the other names I like META if it can reclaim the 704 on the higher timeframes and MSFT Higher TF as well for continuation lower.

text:
Gameplan February 7th 

Lots of volatility coming into yesterdays close plus todays open with unemployment. You can see that there are pretty big ranges with unclear direction on the lower timeframes. So what we will do coming into market open is just wait for the first 15-30 minutes to play out. 

As for names that I will be looking for. TSLA around the 374 on the higher timeframes, NVDA is now inside of the gap level we can be looking for an opening play on this one right off of the bat off 128.34, and I really like META for this flat top break on the higher timeframes. 

As for AMZN stay away from this name right off of the bat. The IV is going to be super juiced up and both sides are going to get crushed. 

As for AAPL I need to see a break above the 233 on the hourly chart If we are  going to push back towards the upside. 

Really today the gameplan is just to wait until we see a name with clear relative strength or  weakness. I do expect the markets to gravatate higher off of the bat but its going to be hard to long right into a key resistance level.

text:
Gameplan February 11th 

Red folder news today with Powell speaking. Right now you can see that the market is gapping down right into PDL's. That is going to be the POI coming into today. I want to see the reaction that we have off of that level. We are also going to get two gaps on the chart. One from over the weekend and another from this morning.

TSLA and NVDA I would be cautious of today. Dead smack inside of the range compared to the overall markets. 

As for the rest of the tickers I would be cautious as there hasn't been as much volatility on those names as of late.

Since now markets are breaking towards the PDL or underneath the PDL what I would like to see is the reaction off those levels coming into market open. Gameplan April 1st

Key watches today will be TSLA. Keep an eye out on the PDH level on this name. NVDA off the 109. 

AAPL I would be cautious inside of the PDH and PDL. Most likely inside bar.

text:
Coming into today another big gap in the markets. You can see that we had news and now we are up around 3% on the major indices. 

We have major gaps towards the upside that were filled in the pre market. Coming into today what I would like to see after this big move higher is the first dip to be bought up. So far the market is moving higher. So I would like to see a pullback in the pre market or a dip during market hours. 

If the market just moves higher right off the bat then we will look for another opening play. 

SPY and QQQ are my main watch for a trade up in torwards the April 15th highs.

As for TSLA be patient on this one right off the bat. Let the IV cool off before trading this name. 

NVDA I like this name above the 104, AAPL hold of the 206, I like AMD as well for a move higher along with PLTR. 

As for the rest of the names just keep an eye out for the key levels that it recliamed for levels of support. @everyone

Coming into today you can see we had a nice push in the power hour yesterday towards ATHs. Now in the premarket we are back at the highs. 

What I would like to see coming into today is the reaction that we have off the PDH key level. 

SPY key level is the 685.5 and the QQQ PMH 629.5. I would be a lot more cautious today right off the bat. 

Similar gameplan to yesterday. You would like to see the hold of key levels. 

As for the main watches. Most of the names will be for day 2 continuation. 

AAPL opening drive towards the upsides, NVDA above the PDH. AMD reclaim above the 258.5. TSLA hold above the 455. 

As for the rest of the names keep and eye out for the PDH key levels. 

@everyone

Gameplan Janaury 26th 

Coming into this week we have a bunch of red folder news with the fed speaking and of course earnings week. Coming into today we had a gap down with news over the weekend but now we are back at the last weeks close. 

What I would like to see coming into market open is the reaction that we have off the 620.5 on the QQQ and the 688.5 on the SPY. Overall markets still holding up very nicely. 

As for the main watches coming into today the names that have the best moves are MSFT, AMZN, & META. These ones had a nice push on Friday. Most of them have earnings this week.

As for the SEMIs I would be a bit cautious. Seems like they are losing a bit of steam. Most of the names are at ATHs. We need to see some sort of pullback or seutp to form in order to take AMD, NVDA, MU, SNDK.

We will be patient today with the market gap down and come into the markets with no bias and just wait for the reaction that we have off key levels.

Gameplan March 14th 

Consumer Sentiment today at 10:00AM EST. With this gap in the markets we are going to be waiting for this today. Every pop has been shorted and we will continue to look for pop and fades. 

Key levels coming into market open are the 476 on the QQQ and 558 on SPY. What I would like to see is the reaction off those levels coming into 10:00AM 

As for the main watches today it will be NVDA. This one is showing strength compared to the markets. What I would like to see is consolidation right off the bat or pullback on this name. Lets see if the first pullback gets bought up. 

TSLA key levels are going to be 242. Also keep an eye out for the PDH on this one. 

AAPL still staying heavy keep an eye out for the reaction off the 211.24 for a pop and fade. 

For the rest of the names keep and eye out for the markets. 

Remember its a Friday plus we have red folder at 10:00AM 

@everyone

In terms of day trades I personally wouldn’t want to go short on anything when everything is HTF bullish because that’s when you see those v shape recoveries and get stuck!

Hope this clears some stuff up for people and what to focus on!

Hey guys!

Want to make one thing clear,

if you are RED today DO NOT be upset.

Look at the price action in the pic below.

That's QQQ.

It did NOTHING.

All range / chop action, every hod/lod came back in the range.

It was a difficult day to trade, the market always has cycles where it's very easy (last 2-3 months) then it will get difficult for 1-2 weeks and then it'll go back.

Once you understand these cycles you'll learn when to be aggressive and defensive OR when to play HTF vs LTF.

With this being said tonight's youtube video will help alot of you guys out that got caught up in the chop.

5PM EST, see y'all then!

author: TonyMontana
text:
Today was one of those days where every single trade I took worked and the thesis was right but timing was off.

This will happen from time to time where you can see after we traded every single trade hit profit target.

It’s important to not let that cloud your ability to trade.

Could I have entered those reclaims and make my money back.

Yes, I knew PLTR was gonna hit HOD with high prob after that 5m pullback.

But for me what’s more important:

Hoping to win my money back or following my rules every single day and letting the money come based off the process of those actions.

The answer is following my rules.

Great lesson today.

@everyone

author: TonyMontana
text:
HOW TO USE UNDERLYING TICKER AS HARD STOP FOR OPTIONS ON IBKR:

1. right click on option position in portfolio
2. select order ticket
3. in the basic tab of the quote panel, choose action (buy or sell), quantity of contracts, and order type (market will execute as take profit or stop loss at market price of option)
4. in the conditional tab, press the add button
5. choose condition Price, next
6. in the underlying text box, type the name of the ticker of the underlying stock (TSLA for example and press enter. this should bring up the security lookup screen. Select Stock (SMART)
7. enter operator and Price. For example, for stop loss, enter the price of the stop and the
operator ＜=
8. press the FINISH button
9. set the logic column to "or"
10. repeat steps 6,7,8,9 entering the take profit price and using the
>= operator
11. Press the "Accept" button in the order ticket quote panel
12. review the trade you just entered in the orders panel to ensure everything is correct
13. press the transmit button

author: Kam
text: if trading options, have to accept some asymmetrical risk on both sides because of the impact of greeks on how the options are priced. Especially with the IV as high as it is on options pricing in the markets right now due to elevated volatility. This looks like the TSLA trade from a couple days ago - if trade is going sideways or against you the IV+theta will kill the options value very fast. The flip side to this is when you get a move in your favor, can make exponential / asymmetric returns also. remember, options value acccelerates the further price moves away fro your strike price. in this case, you didn't really get that aggressive acceleration on the down move - sort of chopped down. unfortunately on the move back up to your stop, the price did move fast in the wrong direction

author: 305 Trader
text: gm. Yeah, symptoms of a fomo trade. We all have those, and typically does not go well. I refrain from going long at a premium level (overextended impulse) or inversely at discount levels, going short. In that case, I like waiting for the stock to retrace to 33- 50% of the impulse and with a STRONG price action and a solid area of support formed there (if formed), decide if the continuation is likely.  Side note, AAPL is a stock that generally likes to consolidate, so that surge most likely needed an immediate period of consolidation with the stock.

text:
Hi

I wanted to share 3 trades I made yestarday, allowing me to make a relatively small profit as I only trade with 1 contracts. 

#1 HOOD 5m low retest with a low risk just above the candle which broke the ORB. TP was a psychological number of 72.00. Unfortunately at 10:34 it hit 72.01 (!) and went back up so I chickened out and took some profits but this trade would have worked out nicely if I had the balls to hold it. Need to work on this part. This would have been a nice 1:3.14 RR and even more as it went further down to $71.50-ish and $71-ish later on.

#2 TSLA premarket high retest with low risk just below the PMH level and TP at 320.00 round level. There was a nice volume spike on the breakout candle and a quick reaction on the retest so I decided to enter at 11:10 candle. Of course I chickened out and didn't stay till it hit my target but got an easy 1:2 RR. This was a 1:5 RR opportunity for me.

#3 GOOGL a couple of retests really: 1m opening candle, 5m range and a pre-market high. This one is the strangest trades I've ever came across, it suddenly spiked up due to some news I believe, however my risk was also very low here with 1 con, just below the 9:43 candle and I was simply aiming for a 1:2 RR. I took profits somewhere around $178.30 level as, again, I chickened out with my 1 con to run. 


I believe I had decent setups, but I just keep screwing up my exits due to fear of loosing profits. Any feedback would be appreciated.

text:
Another trade review request guys 🙏 

today I entered couple of trades I wanted to share and highlight just how important it is to grow some balls and hold onto your trades and stick to your TP:

#1 PLTR was breaking above PDH, PMH and PWH, once it broke the 5m opening range high at 10:24 and immediately retested the next candle it showed strength and so I entered at 10:26 candle with a 1:2 RR target. I took 1 138 call contract but wasn't able to execute sell at target and essentially went out near 10:28 candle close.

#2 HOOD was over 5m opening range high and was also reclaiming PMH with 84% rule at 10:28. This is where I entered looking for 1:2 RR and HOD, maybe even prev day high if it would have showed some strength. I exited at 10:37 as it was not showing enough strenght for me to be convinced to stay in the trade. 

#3 AVGO was showing a lot of strenght as it was above PDH, PMH, also a beautiful 5m opening range B&R (which I missed). There was an order block retest at 10:08 at which I entered with a very low risk just below the 9:59 candle, looking for HOD but hoping for a Friday 6th highs which would be 1:3.5 RR. I exited at 10:23 as it was not showing too much strength and I was afraid of loosing profit as the contract value was drying up.

text: Hey Kash! I think that's a pretty good trade based on the intraday pivot / OB and HTF level reclaim. Honestly I wouldn't nitpick this too much (probabilities), but a couple of things you may want to consider is that it was the exact 10am candle (red folder time) which can be prone to fakeouts in either direction. The stop here is also pretty wide (1 point) so would have to size down to below the hammer/retest candle if presumably you didn't want to enter before red folder.T he market context was a little sus also - Q's strong(er), SPY divergent, but arguably that was nullified by the big PLTR RS at the open. But yeah, the thesis you had at the HTF level was obviously the right one since that was the right evel for the 84 later in the day

author: 305 Trader
text:
hi Francine. I thought of making a review to your trade, because I found it pretty good a teaching for me. You got the direction right, as you can see Apple had been on a upward ride for days. So, yes momentum had been there, thats 1. Now as for your entry, since AAPL demonstrated that the uptrend was clear for several days, that bounce from your wedge in purple lines was your POI and not the ORB you drew. Additionally, the break out from that wedge had confluence with one of your KL. This was a powerful event you should have not missed.  If I was to take a swing or even a day trade on AAPL, it would have been on the break and retest (in a smaller tf) of that confluence. In the higher timeframe (swing) this was also, the continuation signal of the market in its uptrend. So, your entry was late when you decided to make it off of that ORB way above. 
Or, if taking the swing off of that ORB, it would need to be after the mitigation with a strong rejection to that POI or ORB you drew. I think you took it on the 1st impulse instead  and hence you had the expected pullback. I am curious how the symbol did on Friday since I had not traded since last Tuesday.

author: Ruslan /ruˈslan/
text:
Guys, I want to share my crappy day because of my own stupidity. The story is actually kind of funny 🙂
I took 1 TSLA 302.5 Put 0DTE contract, held it the whole time while the price was falling, and as soon as it reversed after 298, I couldn’t sell—like hypnotized—waiting for it to go back down, all the way until it climbed up to 301.5, and only then did I lock in a $30 profit, even though I could’ve made a few hundred bucks.
And then classic: I immediately jumped into a revenge trade and locked in a $70 loss.
I thought I’d learned to get out on a mental stop-loss (sometimes it’s tough mentally, especially after red days), but I didn’t expect myself to hesitate and not take the profit.
Just wanted to share the reflection 🙂
To everyone who’s green today—respect. And to those who aren’t—also, because we’re still here and still trying to get better.

author: Anne
text:
I made many mistakes today as I was emotionally driven:
I entered very early (which I have to stop doing) (9:33)on NVDIA with Jack. Next mistake on this trade: I did not wait for the confirmation candle to close. So I lost on this trade (-130$) when I exited at 9:55. I was already very unhappy with myself and felt the urge for revenge trading. I did not do it immediately, but my next two trades were not done according to the process focused trading I learn here in this group.
Then at 9:48 I entered HOOD on its immediate retest of 5 min high. This time I waited for the confirmation candle to close. I was red with that for the next 8 minutes which made me emotions become much stronger then my reason. I scaled out as soon as I was green, the last con I sold at 10:03. In regard to the process this moves are not good at all because I had no candle close below my stop loss. If I had been stronger than my emotions I would have won my loss back while HOOD moved up from this minute on.
While I was fighting with my emotions I entered TSLA listening to Tony. The price action was strong, so I got a bad entry. It moved in my risk area for ten mins which I could not digest. When it moved up I exited quickly for not to take another loss today. Especially these TSLA losses are heavy. And then I saw the stock move up really nice.

author: Royal191
text: Hi Anne, glad to see you are able to identify the issue so quickly. Now you can make a plan/rules to avoid this happening in the future. Revenge trading is one of those things that will wreck your mental capital and your actual capital. Especially revenge trading with names like TSLA or META. If you take a bad trade, try to step away from the screens for a few mins and clear your head. If you decide to come back and look for another trade you have to treat the next trade as its own trade and trade it without the emotions from the prev trades. Once you have the prev loss in your mind it will be easier to make mistakes like taking profits too early or even holding too long to make up the loss and letting a green trade turn red.

author: jav
text: Hey Max, I am certainly not someone to be giving advice but somethings I have learned and advice I have been given that you may find useful. In regards to a mental stop or a hard stop, with a hard stop if the candle hits your stop area your going to be stopped out of the trade, which is why Tony and Jack always say to wait for candle closure. I used to always use a hard stop but I would mostly get stopped out and then the stock would take off in the way I wanted it to, which can be very nerve racking. I am not sure what your set up was on those 2 trades but Tony advises you to stay with one set up when you are a new trader, whether that be the 5 minute opening range, premarket or previous day and just stay with whichever your most comfortable with. I personally only trade the 5 minute opening range break. I also switched to a 5 minute chart because trading off a 1 minute chart I found to be super stressful. The only con to a 5 minute chart when waiting for candle closure is if you get a big candle the opposite of your trade your stop is going to be much lower than you wanted it to be, but that has only happened once in TSLA.  I hope you found something useful in this and good luck in your trading journey.

author: Neto Moreno (Performance Coach)
text:
What could you tweak next time?

1. Pre-define your invalidation before entry (you did this ✅).
2. If price snaps back under the level in the next 1-3 candles → ask:
   - Is the setup still clean? (structure, volume, QQQ correlation)
   - Am I calm enough to re-enter? (stress = red flag)

If yes → second-chance entry at the same or tighter risk is often higher probability (fakeout flushed weak hands).
But only if you’re calm. Stress = skip it.

LOD would have been the first scale and you can see at LOD at 9:51 Qs was bouncing and reclaiming key levels to the upside which was trying to push TSLA back up.
Hopefully that makes sense

1. NVDA likes to do this recently so we have to be aggressive in scaling out
2. Do not wait for Jack or Tony to say that they have entered. It might already be too late by then for quicker scalpes with little to no continuation.

author: Kam
text:
One thing I would encourage is 'zooming out'. While the technical level was there, the overall context for this trade idea wasn't as good as looking for a long trade on QQQ if you trade indices. 

There's been pretty clear divergence between QQQ and SPY, and with Q's opening above PDH and in new ATH territory, there was far less resistance than on SPY which is still inside the prior 2 day range. 

On the technical side - there isn't much displacement above PDH which I would consider the main level here, the price action on the reclaim also doesn't look too convincing given it just chopped down through the level. 

Same concept on the 2nd trade; the PA more convincing there - but is that trade worth the R/R? 

<@1325884177291280475> goes over a lot of these concepts in his daily coaching calls - would definitely check out the recording or attend if you can

author: Martin_AT
text:
Hello,
on Friday my overall bias was correct because my bias was to the downside. QQQ dropped after market open and was below PDL but I still hesitated to go short on AMD. I missed the first two order block retest opportunities. On the third order block retest I already had a bad feeling but I still went short. The trade was a looser but after 11:10 am price continued to go down.
https://www.tradingview.com/x/9jDs9Idd/
For me the learning is this (more like a "re-learning" because I should have known this): If Qs is dropping for about 30min without a significant pullback then the chance for a bigger pullback or a reversal is too high and therefore shorting stocks on the 1min TF is too high risk. Thus in future I would focus on shorting opportunities at the beginning of the session and avoid late short opportunities like AMD von Friday. (Based on all the trade reviews from Tony/Jack that I have watched I noticed that they never go short too late - like me in this case)

What are your thoughts on this? Do guys also avoid late entries or is there something else I missed? Thanks

author: 305 Trader
text: you are missing a key element, in your analysis. Its the HTF. In the 1H TF and 4H Tf identify strong levels of support and resistance (often are pivot points), and plan your trades on the reaction to those levels, as well as use them to identify your exits. That move most certainly in AMD hit an important support level at 486 in 1H Tf. Take a look and you may see this. Do not trade if you dont make a thesis based on laying out a plan on these two HTF.

I maybe should not Post this now because I am so confused.

Tony's recent Post says that this week has been a "fantastic week of trading" and "this market is not something we want to miss".

I am not criticizing him, or this channel, or anyone. I just do not understand. I know he explains why he takes things, but...well... please read on before you Comment.

It seems that "we" were taking INTC again today (and I can clearly see the INTC trade on the INTC chart), but I do not see support for any Long trade on the QQQ 1m TF at the time of the INTC trade.

I considered the second area, but noticed Sellers kept pushing it down, and then noticed the purple resistance line. I called it quits on another red day.

So, can anyone help me understand how QQQ supported the INTC (and AMD) trade when it was heading south and below all the levels on the 1m TF ?
And, what was wrong with my QQQ trade idea ?

text:
Hey <@717554586843611217> , I am not an experienced and profitable trader like you however I would like to point out some obvious observations overlooked on this NVDA trade today.
1.    On HTFs this was a gap fill and reject (daily gap) + Hourly 200EMA (rejected 3-4 times from there) sitting right there as a confluence
2.    QQQ opened very close to or in HTF supply and never broke above PDH’s 
3.    These 2 confluences above were strong enough to not enter this trade per my observation
4.    I found this trade impulsive rather than thoughtful based on HTFs
Hope you don’t take this negatively.

author: Aleksandra Seliverstova
text:
I kinda count the risk per trade, to have equal risk per trade in all trades - 150$. Still I lost 294$ on Monday (150$ standard risk times 2 losses), 98$ yesterday (1 loss which was larger than expected, because half of the position I sold at breakeven), and today with pretty same risk amount I gained 24$ on 1 con AMD (sold at low of day) and 57$ on 3 cons AAPL (sold part at low of day and part a bit lower). 
How do you guys manage your risk to actually be profitable with, for instance, 2:1 win rate? I end up needing like 4:1 win rate with such stats, in order to be profitable.
I use market orders, maybe that's the reason - I buy a bit more expensive and sell a bit cheaper and with a small RR it ends up eating huge part of the profit

author: byakuyako1
text:
NEWS:

The space and defense firm, Firefly Aerospace $FLY is looking to land a $5.5 billion valuation in its U.S. IPO, aiming to raise up to $631.8 million by pricing shares between $35 and $39.

Tesla $TSLA has signed a $16.5B deal with Samsung to produce its next-gen AI6 chips at the company’s upcoming fab in Taylor, Texas. Musk says he’ll walk the line himself to help optimize production, calling the deal “strategically important.” Samsung’s foundry, which has struggled with under-utilization, now gets a major boost. The agreement runs through 2033, and Musk hinted the total output could be “several times higher” than the headline figure.

$AMD has reportedly raised the price of its MI350 AI chip by $10K to $25,000 - newsis

HSBC evaluated that "MI350 can now compete with $NVDA's Blackwell B200 in the market," & "AMD's AI chip sales next year will be significantly higher than the prior estimate of $9.6B, at $15.1B"

OPPENHEIMER RAISES S&P 500 TARGET TO 7,100 FROM 5,950 

Oppenheimer restored its year-end S&P 500 target to 7,100, up from 5,950 in April, thanks to new trade deals with Japan and the EU easing market uncertainty. This implies an 11% gain from the July 25 close.

$NVDA - NVIDIA'S H20 CHIP SUPPLY CAN'T MATCH CHINA'S SOARING DEMAND: JEFFERIES

Jefferies says Nvidia’s H20 AI chip stockpile (600K–900K units) falls short of China’s demand, which could hit 1.8M units, following a temporary easing of U.S. export restrictions.

Despite supply limits, Chinese firms prefer Nvidia chips due to its CUDA ecosystem, superior performance, and limited local alternatives.

Jefferies expects strong demand to continue—even for downgraded future chips like the upcoming B30 (Q4 2025). It raised China’s 2025 AI capex forecast by 40% to $108B, with no sign of slowing AI investments.

author: 305 Trader
text: Whenever the ORB of 5 min is inside the PDR, extra caution has to be exerted and observe a lot PA. The video released on Saturday by Jdub Trades is vital to form a Bias and a narrative. This will help you stay focused on what your trading day and the marker forces will aim for, but w/o being too rigid that it has to be that way. Remember the market does what it wants to do. We just need to observe. A lot of people lost with TSLA today, if you take a look at the 5 min ORB for TSLA, you see a body with long tails. This warns of market chop. If you dont have a narrative and that is the symbol you like to trade, watch the 5 min and 15 min TF in your monitors. Wait. Only enter upon a solid confirmation of Buyers or sellers conviction but always remembering your narrative. This is what I did. I saw I needed extra confirmation to take an entry and the reason I won is because I did my homework and drew KL and had a narrative formed before the market opened.

author: Markellwhite16
text: I see where you’re coming from. A couple  of things .. never predict . Our job is to react not predict. When you predict you go into the market with a bias and force trades. I am 100% bullish on PLTR until it breaks a key level on the HTF that causes a break of structure. You don’t wanna be the trader that keeps trying to short the highs and get smoked. The trend is your friend is a real thing. Look at names like MU , ORCl , even QQQ & SPY. Week in and out these names keep making new highs. PLTR can easily rip through its ATH , pull back , retest that level and continue higher. The last 2 days on this name has been a ROCKET 🚀! So my best advice is don’t go into the market trying to “predict” the exact top where a reversal might occur. Just keep taking what the market gives you.

text: Part of it is momentum. Tony and Jack always say “scale on pops! Or scale on strength!” That’s because the contracts are juiced in those moments and they provide a nicer market value. author: 305 Trader
text:
good morning Patel. Do not go hard on yourself. Your value is not defined by 2x losses. Not by 10x or even 20x losses. If you develop a trading plan and you adhere to it, that discipline will define you. Trading is a business where focus on zoom out and zoom in is needed. Fight FOMO, a falling move can also be a falling knife. This particular dump in SPY in its first leg as per your screenshot did not offer an A+ set up in my view for the following reasons:

- 1st reaction candle, too large. Increasing the Stop loss unnecessarily if you like to wait for a confirmation candle.
- your 2nd set up, no proper mitigation, just friction and the entry at LOD. 

“Not everything that shines is gold”, its an old spanish saying. Become picky, selective and forget about the profits that people post everyday, it is your journey and your money.

author: Joebag009
text: Thank you for taking the time to reply to my specific question, hearing that from a pro means a lot! I have noticed psychologically I start getting nervous when positions are over 8K, even if a good chunk of my total account is not deployed. My capital is 30K and that gives me 100K buy power in the margin account. I try not to have any position over 10K, except for plain shares of indexes in a day trade (slower move = same risk as small leveraged position). Positions of 2-6K are a comfort zone, and at that size risking 50 to make 100 hits hard! On a day trade if I see it -50 I get nervous and if it is close to +100 I'm pumping that "sell" button like a senior at a casino machine handle. I am starting to get comfortable with a single option on QQQ. Compared to the pro traders who do one or two setups a day, I take many many trades with ridiculously low risk tolerance and quick cashouts. It is tedious but has given me consistent green week after week. text: Hey <@1402284752110882909>, once the market opens the day after earnings, the IV is going to be very high on the options contracts. Say we were looking to go long on TSLA the day after earnings, in order for us to go long we need to see some big red candles because those candles will crush the "call options'" IV, making it go way down. When you play names with very high IV the R:R never makes sense because usually you're risking a lot more money to make a smaller ammount. Hope that helps

author: Huy
text: i wrote a few things about this before. I dropped a lot of good advices on here so you can search my name and scan through it. Sorry you have to experience it like this but this is proof why trading is really up to you. You are in the driver seat. 100 traders can enter the same trade at the exact same time but all get difference results. Do what works for you even if that means not going after that 1:2 rr that everyone has been preaching. Look into 1:1 rr. I think as of late, only half of their trades got more than 1:2 rr. What does this mean for you with 1 contract? You can easily get caught in the unfavorable probabilities. What I personally do is i aim to take 50-70% off at 1:1rr then aim for 1:2 for the rest. A thing you can also do is avoid trading tickers that are expensive like TSLA and MU where you can only afford one contract. Also if you can only trade with 1-3 contracts, your timing is everything so work on reading price action.

author: Hana
text:
Yesterday I lost $3K — a little over half my account. MU and ASTS dropped hard and my contracts were down about 60%.

The trade felt valid… until it wasn’t.

What’s messing with me is that hours later the move actually came. That’s the part that hits mentally more than the loss itself.

Now my account is at $1,600 and I’m honestly asking:

How are we supposed to react in moments like this?

Do you just accept it and move on?
Do you laugh it off?
Do you sit with it and reflect?
Or do you regret not holding and wonder “what if”?

Because holding to -80% hoping for a reversal… that’s not easy either. Most people would’ve been wiped before seeing that move.

I know I sized bigger than I should have — and I’ll own that. But I’m really curious how you all handle this mentally when it happens.

author: DHayesTrades
text: Hey guys - I'm fairly new here been tradig in the community for  afew weeks now. An issue I keep running into is the stop losses. They seem to be fairly discretionary. Today was the perfect example on NVDA. I entered when I saw clear buyers stepping in on the Wednesday Highs level retest - it then reverses and had two candles testing it. Both candles broke that level (where my stop loss was) but both candles did not close underneath. I stopped out when it broke. The trade then runs amazingly without me lol. Cand someone please inform me how to successfully place and respect the stop losses around these key levels especially during a candle trying to break it?

author: JP400
text: Hi. I am new here too. I think you said it yourself... the  Stops are discretionary. I too had a Stop probably around the same place on NVDA. If it had been a Stop Loss Order, it would have filled, and I would have lost. But, I choose to Stop out by hovering over the Sell button. If the candle closes below my Stop with weakness, I sell. If it closes below, with a tail (buyers coming in), I may hold. That is what happened today. So I held. But... as you said.. it is at my discretion.  I am still debating if that is the right idea for me. Sometimes the candle dives below my Stop, and I take a loss that is larger than I wanted. I do not trade many Contracts, so I then struggle to recover that. People that buy 10's of Contracts could recover on their next trade. I am not sure if that is what you are asking.... text:
Gameplan for 04 June 2026

We have a gap down on some semis and memory names which dragged down the indices overnight. 
Will be watching the reaction around key levels. SPY around PDL and PMH along with 749 area. QQQ around 735-736 area, below PML we have room towards 730 and below.

For the main watches- don't like a lot on semis and memory for longs as its down quite a bit. Below PDL on a lot of names and don't want to short those names either due to HTF.

Couple of names that I like at the moment are-
AAPL above PMH
MSFT above PMH - we are sitting on HTF support and showing some strength in pre market 
GOOGL below 356 area

Secondary watches-
TSLA above 424.80 
NVDA above 217.50 we have room towards PDH
MU if we reclaim PDL

author: kython89
text: In a recent video Tony talked about why the B&R can fail and showed an example of going against the Daily Chart / HTF trend.  It seems like most the trades they were considering today were against the tickers Daily trend yet they considered / took them anyways.  The INTC obviously didn't work out.  Calls on Amazon ended up working out but it was against the HTF trend.  It seems like patience was the correct choice today and had Tony practiced what he taught in the YouTube video he could have avoided the loss?  They teach use a mechanical system but when it comes down to live trading it seems like for every rule there is an exception and it all comes down to discretionary choices not a mechanical process.

author: Apex Trader
text:
hey kython, a couple things to factor in. when tony took that trade SMH was trending down (hold all semi conductors) this would be used more in conjunction to the trade than qqq/spy in general.

on top of this MU earnings, context wise if mu is weak this morning (it was) you can’t trade that but you can trade the next weak ticker which would be intc in this case.

ofc, yes the trade lost but it was still systematic and within the system if context was understood.
